## Visualization Document

Working document for all of the visualizations used for the DS-403 (Digital Humanities) project. Parsing in text data, for analysis of thematic patterns throughout the various translations of Homer's *The Odyssey*.

## Research Question:

How do the vocabulary choices throughout the three different translations of Homer's *The Odyssey* influence the narrative being communicated; and does it capture the core themes of the original story?

## Hypothesis:

I predict that the text data from the different translations will reveal some of the core themes from *The Odyssey* through the vocabulary that is used within each translation. However, how much overlap between the translations is a different story. If i were to draw preliminary conclusions, I would guess that the first two translations of *The Odyssey* that were published chronologically (so in this case Fagles, and Fitzgerald) will have more in common than the most recent translation (Wilson). I predict this because the newer translation was created with the goal of appealing to the modern generation of readers. Another thing is that I think the core themes of the original Odyssey story will be more in tact in older versions because the translators/authors were not working to push specific agendas. Wilson's translation was the backbone of the script for the Christopher Nolan's *The Odyssey* (2026) and the movie alone took many creative liberties with the character interpretations. That being said, if the Wilson translation is anything like the film in terms of what narrative it conveys and how it depicts the characters, I think the vocabulary words that are parsed by the text-mining will reveal a lack of overlap between some core themes compared to the other two (older) translations.

## Progress:

Currently I have no visualizations but I have solidified my sources, uploaded them to this repository and also installed all of the text mining packages provided by Dr. Chong.

## Assigning the start and end for when to parse text data

```{r}
check_ranges <- function(pdf_files, page_ranges, n_chars = 300) {
  for (name in names(pdf_files)) {
    pages <- pdf_text(pdf_files[[name]])
    s <- page_ranges[[name]][["start"]]
    e <- page_ranges[[name]][["end"]]
    if (is.na(s)) s <- 1
    if (is.na(e)) e <- length(pages)
    
    cat("\n=====", name, "| total pages in PDF:", length(pages),
        "| range:", s, "-", e, "=====\n")
    cat("--- START (page", s, ") ---\n")
    cat(substr(str_squish(pages[s]), 1, n_chars), "\n")
    cat("--- END (page", e, ") -
        --\n")
    last <- str_squish(pages[e])
    cat(substr(last, max(1, nchar(last) - n_chars), nchar(last)), "\n")
  }
}

check_ranges(pdf_files, page_ranges)
```

```{r}
read_translation <- function(path, translator, start = NA, end = NA) {
  pages <- pdf_text(path)
  n <- length(pages)
  s <- ifelse(is.na(start), 1, start)
  e <- ifelse(is.na(end), n, end)
  pages <- pages[s:e]
  
  # One row per line of text
  tibble(translator = translator,
         page = seq(s, e),
         text = pages) |>
    mutate(text = str_split(text, "\n")) |>
    unnest(text)
}

raw_lines <- imap_dfr(pdf_files, function(path, name) {
  read_translation(path, name,
                   start = page_ranges[[name]][["start"]],
                   end   = page_ranges[[name]][["end"]])
})
```

```{r}
raw_lines |> group_by(translator) |>
  summarise(lines = n(), characters = sum(nchar(text)))
```

## Huge Clean Sesh from Claude (Ayo?)

```{r}
# =============================================================================
# UPDATE 1 of 3: REPLACE the entire old "Section 3. Clean the text" with this
# (everything from "# ---- 3. Clean the text" down to and including the old
#  odyssey_full <- ... block). Run it right after Section 2 (raw_lines).
# =============================================================================

# ---- 3. Clean the text (tailored to the Fitzgerald, Fagles, Wilson PDFs) ----

# A "Book" heading: "BOOK ONE: A GODDESS INTERVENES" (Fitzgerald),
# "Book I" (Fagles), "BOOK 1" (Wilson). Case-sensitive on purpose so a verse
# line that happens to start with "book" is not mistaken for a heading.
# Fitzgerald's PDF splits letters ("BOOK T WENT Y-ONE", "BOOK SEV EN"), so the
# number part allows any capitals, digits, spaces and hyphens before the colon.
book_heading_rx <- "^(BOOK|Book)\\s+[A-Z0-9 -]+(:.*)?$"

# Running headers / front-matter lines to delete, per translation.
# Add patterns here if you spot more leftovers (see the checks below).
header_rx <- list(
  Fitzgerald = c("^[0-9]+_[0-9]+-[0-9]+_",   # production line: "05_273-611_Homer 2/Aesop ... Page 273"
                 "^H ?OMER\\s*/",            # running header: "H OMER / The Odyssey, Book One 273"
                 "^THE ODYSSEY$",
                 "^Translated by"),
  Fagles     = character(0),
  Wilson     = character(0)
)

clean_translation <- function(df, tr) {
  
  # Step A: squish whitespace, drop bare page numbers and running headers
  d <- df |>
    mutate(text = str_squish(text)) |>
    filter(!str_detect(text, "^[0-9]+$"))
  
  if (length(header_rx[[tr]]) > 0) {
    d <- d |> filter(!str_detect(text, paste(header_rx[[tr]], collapse = "|")))
  }
  
  # Step B: group consecutive non-blank lines into blocks (a paragraph,
  # stanza, heading, footnote...). Blank lines separate blocks.
  d <- d |>
    mutate(is_blank   = text == "",
           block      = cumsum(is_blank != lag(is_blank, default = TRUE)),
           is_heading = str_detect(text, book_heading_rx)) |>
    group_by(block) |>
    mutate(block_first       = first(text),
           block_has_headnote = any(str_detect(text, "Editors.{0,3}headnote"))) |>
    ungroup()
  
  # Blocks that sit right after a heading and are the book's subtitle
  # (Fagles: "Athena Inspires / the Prince"; Wilson: "The Boy and the Goddess").
  # Non-blank blocks alternate with blank ones, so the subtitle is heading + 2.
  heading_blocks <- unique(d$block[d$is_heading])
  
  d <- d |>
    mutate(
      book = cumsum(is_heading),    # 0 = anything before Book 1 (intro, etc.)
      drop_block =
        block %in% heading_blocks |                                       # whole heading block, incl. wrapped title lines
        block_has_headnote |                                              # editors' headnotes (Fitzgerald)
        (tr == "Fitzgerald" & str_detect(block_first, "^[0-9]{1,3} \\S")) |  # footnote paragraphs
        (tr %in% c("Fagles", "Wilson") & block %in% (heading_blocks + 2))    # book subtitles
    ) |>
    filter(book > 0, !drop_block, !is_heading, !is_blank)
  
  # Step C: tidy the remaining verse lines
  d |>
    mutate(text = str_replace_all(text, "[\u2018\u2019]", "'"),     # curly -> straight quotes
           text = str_replace_all(text, "[\u201C\u201D]", "\""),
           text = str_replace_all(text, "[\u2013\u2014]", " "),     # dashes -> space (avoids glued words)
           text = str_remove(text, "\\s+[0-9]{1,4}$"),              # line numbers / footnote markers at end
           text = str_remove(text, "^[0-9]{1,4}\\s+"),              # numbers at start
           text = stringi::stri_trans_general(text, "Latin-ASCII"), # Telemakhos accents -> plain letters
           text = str_squish(text)) |>
    filter(text != "") |>
    select(translator, book, page, text)
}

odyssey_lines <- raw_lines |>
  group_split(translator) |>
  map_dfr(~ clean_translation(.x, unique(.x$translator)))

# Full text per translator (used for sentence and bigram tokenizing)
odyssey_full <- odyssey_lines |>
  group_by(translator) |>
  summarise(text = paste(text, collapse = " "), .groups = "drop")

# ---- 3b. Checks: run these and look before moving on ------------------------

# (1) How many book headings were detected in the raw text? Expect 24 for a
#     full translation. Fewer means an excerpted edition or a heading pattern
#     that did not match.
raw_lines |>
  mutate(t = str_squish(text)) |>
  filter(str_detect(t, book_heading_rx)) |>
  count(translator, name = "headings_found")

# (2) Size of the cleaned text per translator
odyssey_lines |>
  group_by(translator) |>
  summarise(books = n_distinct(book),
            lines = n(),
            words = sum(str_count(text, "\\S+")))

# (3) First lines of Book 1 should be the opening of the poem
odyssey_lines |> filter(book == 1) |> group_by(translator) |> slice(1:4) |> print(n = Inf)

# (4) Unusually long lines are usually leftover prose (notes, summaries, intro)
odyssey_lines |>
  filter(nchar(text) > 75) |>
  select(translator, book, page, text) |>
  print(n = 40)

# (5) Broken ligatures from PDF extraction (e.g. "f light" for "flight")
odyssey_lines |>
  filter(str_detect(text, "\\bf [a-z]")) |>
  select(translator, page, text) |>
  print(n = 20)

# (6) Leftover ALL-CAPS lines (wrapped heading text, stray headers, etc.)
odyssey_lines |>
  filter(str_detect(text, "^[A-Z0-9 ,.'-]{6,}$")) |>
  select(translator, book, page, text) |>
  print(n = 30)

# (7) Fitzgerald only: last page that still has the "HOMER" running header.
#     Use this (or a page just after it) as the `end` in page_ranges so the
#     Aesop material that follows is not read in as part of Book 24.
raw_lines |>
  filter(translator == "Fitzgerald") |>
  mutate(t = str_squish(text)) |>
  filter(str_detect(t, "^H ?OMER /")) |>
  summarise(last_homer_page = max(page))


# =============================================================================

# tidy_words (the one with str_remove_all("^'+|'+$")) with this. It also
# strips possessives, so "Zeus's" and "Zeus'" both count as "zeus".

# Accents are already stripped, so Fitzgerald's Telemakhos / Kirke / Kalypso /
```

## Tokenize

```{r}
# ---- 4. Tokenize ------------------------------------------------------------
tidy_words <- odyssey_lines |>
  unnest_tokens(word, text) |>
  mutate(word = str_remove_all(word, "^'+|'+$")) |>   # trim stray apostrophes
  filter(word != "", !str_detect(word, "\\d"))

# Position of each word within its translation (0 to 1)
tidy_words <- tidy_words |>
  group_by(translator) |>
  mutate(word_index = row_number(),
         position   = word_index / n()) |>
  ungroup()

# Non-stop-word version (for content analysis)
data("stop_words")
custom_stops <- tibble(word = c("thy", "thee", "thou", "thine", "hath", "doth",
                                "shall", "will", "said", "say", "came", "come",
                                "went", "one", "now", "upon", "on", "may"))
content_words <- tidy_words |>
  anti_join(stop_words, by = "word") |>
  anti_join(custom_stops, by = "word")
```

## Basic Visualizations:

```{r}
# ---- 5. Plot 1: Overall length of each translation -------------------------
word_totals <- tidy_words |> count(translator, name = "total_words")

ggplot(word_totals, aes(translator, total_words, fill = translator)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = comma(total_words)), vjust = -0.4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = translator_colors) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(title = "Total Word Count by Translation",
       x = NULL, y = "Words")
```

## More Plots:

```{r}
# ---- 6. Plot 2: Vocabulary richness ----------------------------------------
vocab <- tidy_words |>
  group_by(translator) |>
  summarise(tokens = n(),
            types = n_distinct(word),
            ttr = types / tokens, .groups = "drop")
vocab

ggplot(vocab, aes(translator, types, fill = translator)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = comma(types)), vjust = -0.4) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = translator_colors) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(title = "Unique Vocabulary Size (Distinct Words)",
       x = NULL, y = "Distinct words")

# Vocabulary growth curves (distinct words seen vs. words read)
vocab_growth <- tidy_words |>
  group_by(translator) |>
  mutate(new_word = !duplicated(word),
         types_so_far = cumsum(new_word)) |>
  ungroup()

ggplot(vocab_growth, aes(word_index, types_so_far, color = translator)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = translator_colors) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = comma) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = comma) +
  labs(title = "Vocabulary Growth Curve",
       subtitle = "How quickly each translation introduces new words",
       x = "Words read", y = "Distinct words so far", color = NULL)
```

```{r}
# ---- 8. Plot 4: Line and sentence length -----------------------------------
# Line length (verse structure: Fitzgerald/Fagles/Wilson all differ)
line_stats <- odyssey_lines |>
  mutate(words_in_line = str_count(text, "\\S+"))

ggplot(line_stats, aes(words_in_line, fill = translator)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, color = "white", show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ translator, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = translator_colors) +
  labs(title = "Words per Line of Verse",
       x = "Words in line", y = "Number of lines")

# Sentence length
sentences <- odyssey_full |>
  unnest_tokens(sentence, text, token = "sentences") |>
  mutate(words_in_sentence = str_count(sentence, "\\S+"))

ggplot(sentences, aes(translator, words_in_sentence, fill = translator)) +
  geom_boxplot(show.legend = FALSE, outlier.alpha = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = translator_colors) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 80)) +
  labs(title = "Sentence Length by Translation",
       x = NULL, y = "Words per sentence")

sentences |> group_by(translator) |>
  summarise(mean_len = mean(words_in_sentence),
            median_len = median(words_in_sentence))
```

```{r}
# ---- 12. Plot 8: Word-frequency comparison between translations ------------
# Relative frequency of each word, compared across translators.
freq_wide <- tidy_words |>
  anti_join(stop_words, by = "word") |>
  count(translator, word) |>
  group_by(translator) |>
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(-n) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = translator, values_from = prop, values_fill = 0)

plot_freq_pair <- function(df, x, y) {
  ggplot(df, aes(.data[[x]], .data[[y]])) +
    geom_abline(color = "gray50", lty = 2) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.4, color = "steelblue") +
    geom_text_repel(data = df |> filter(.data[[x]] > 0.002 | .data[[y]] > 0.002),
                    aes(label = word), size = 3, max.overlaps = 15) +
    scale_x_log10(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 0.01)) +
    scale_y_log10(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 0.01)) +
    labs(title = paste(x, "vs.", y, "word frequencies"),
         subtitle = "Words near the dashed line are used equally often",
         x = x, y = y)
}

freq_pos <- freq_wide |> filter(Fitzgerald > 0, Fagles > 0, Wilson > 0)
plot_freq_pair(freq_pos, "Fitzgerald", "Fagles")
plot_freq_pair(freq_pos, "Fitzgerald", "Wilson")
plot_freq_pair(freq_pos, "Fagles", "Wilson")

# Correlation of word usage between translations
freq_pos |> select(-word) |> cor(method = "spearman") |> round(3)
```
